かえりますか.en: What about a grammar point that is used as a part of honorific speech?

おかえりなさるんですか.en: Nice guess! While お〜なさる carries nearly an identical meaning to the grammar point that Bunpro is looking for, it is considered quite archaic and old-fashioned, mainly being found in literary work up to the end of the Edo period.

おかえりなさいます.en: Let's try a grammar pattern that is a bit more old-fashioned.

おかえりなさいますか.en: Let's try a grammar pattern that is a bit more old-fashioned.

おかえりです.en: How about a grammar pattern that is a bit more polite?

かえりになりますか.en: Close! Because this is an honorific expression, we need to add the respectful prefix that often comes before the verb stem in these constructions.

おかえりします.en: する is not used for honorifics like this. We are looking for a different construction which shows respect for the subject's action.

おかえりしますか.en: する is not used for honorifics like this. We are looking for a different construction which shows respect for the subject's action.

おかえりますか.en: You're on the right track with the prefix お, but can you try including something else to show respect toward the subject?

おかえりなります.en: Can you try checking your conjugation?

おかえりなりますか.en: Can you try checking your conjugation?

attributes.nuance_translation: A polite, modern expression, that respectfully states the action of others.

attributes.body:
お～になる (or ご～になる) is an honorific language expression which is used to pay respect to the actions of the person that is being spoken to/another person (never the speaker). In this expression, になる is used in exactly the same way that する would be, except that it will be attached to the ます stem of the verb that it is referring to.

The primary difference between お and ご, is that お will be used with words/readings of Japanese origin (kun-yomi), and ご will be used with words/readings of Chinese origin (on-yomi). In fact, お and ご are both represented by the same kanji. For this kanji, 御（お） is one of the kun-yomi, and 御（ご） is one of the on-yomi.

Fun Fact

Some verbs, like いでる, are used almost exclusively with honorific language. おいでになる (the お～になる form of いでる) is an example of this, and can mean 'to come', 'to go', or 'to be'. This is due to the perspective of the speaker when using honorific language, and something that we will discuss in more detail later.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

attributes.description: お〜になる vs. お〜なさる

attributes.body: These are honorific forms used to respectfully describe others' actions. お～になる is used with regular verbs, e.g. 書く 'write' becoming お書きになる (same meaning, but showing respect to the writer). いらっしゃる is a special honorific form that replaces 行く, 来る, and いる, for which the お～になる form is not used.

second_relatable.title: いらっしゃる
second_relatable.meaning: To be (Honorific), To come (Honorific), To go (Honorific)

attributes.body: Both are honorific forms. お～になる is used for regular verbs, like 答える 'answer' becoming お答えになる (same meaning, but showing respect to the answerer). なさる is the specific honorific form of する, e.g. ゴルフをなさる  means '(He/she) plays golf.' in an honorific/respectful sense. Since する is irregular, it does not use the お～になる pattern.
